title: Replace the stock chain and both sprockets together
completeness: Complete stock13/51 sprocket pair and114-link non-sealed520 chain renewal with one rear-wheel removal/refit, new mechanical retention and measured final chain closure. Existing intact chain and functional rear brake are required for the attributed manual holding method.

source.review_note: Exact OEM54/136/196/198/394 rendered and visually reviewed; previously approved rear-wheel and chain closure reused. Nick Dole authored technical article held on his Teknik Motorsport site, PDF5 printed120, visually reviewed for manual rear-brake holding technique only. Other article suggestions are not adopted. Root independently reviewed all16 steps, OEM196/198/394/137 and Nick DolePDF5. Approved with intact old chain/rear-brake holding scope and explicit clip-diagram link.

applicability.included: Exact stockUS2026YZ450F, OEM13T front9383E-13233 and51T rearB2W-25451-00, stock520 non-sealed114-link clip chain.
excluded: Broken chain or lost tooth engagement preventing brake-reaction holding
Faulty rear brake or damaged hub/shaft splines

required_tools.name: Stable maintenance stand plus stationary bike support and helper for rear-brake holding
Correct front sprocket socket/breaker bar and calibrated torque tools covering7–135Nm
Appropriate tool to unfold/fold locking washer tabs without harming shaft or nut
Rear sprocket bolt holding tool and nut socket, rear axle/adjuster tools
Chain-link clip tools, measuring scale and approximately50N chain lifting force reference
Clean labeled parts storage and protection for disc/pads

required_parts.name: New matching non-sealed520 chain114links, joining link, plate and new clip
required_parts.purpose: New chain with new sprocket pair

required_parts.name: New exact front sprocket lock washer
Six matching new rear sprocket self-locking nuts
required_parts.purpose: Workflow renews locking nuts during pair replacement

required_parts.name: OEM-specified LOCTITE locking agent for front sprocket nut
required_parts.purpose: Grade/cure time not named by OEM; identify actual product and follow its instructions

required_parts.name: Lithium-soap grease and suitable non-sealed chain lubricant

prerequisites: Confirm correct new stock front/rear sprockets and matching new chain/link set before disassembly.
Old chain must remain connected and engage both sprockets sufficiently for a stationary rear-brake holding check; rear brake must work normally. This method does not address a broken/missing chain.
Helper and stable support available for manual torque reaction; transmission neutral, engine stopped throughout.
critical_stop_conditions: Unstable support or old chain/brake cannot hold sprocket without slipping.
Damaged output-shaft splines/threads, hub, brake or wheel components.
Missing washer engagement, unseated joining clip or unresolved binding/misalignment.
entry_state: Assembled stock bike with intact engaged old chain and functional rear brake; exact replacement pair/chain ready.
exit_state: Both new stock sprockets and new matching chain fitted; front90Nm nut retained by new folded washer, rear six42Nm nuts, axle135Nm/adjusters21Nm, cover7Nm and measured50–60mm slack verified.

steps.title: Record the original drive and replacement parts
steps.instruction: Keep the engine stopped and transmission neutral. Support the bike securely. Confirm functional rear brake and intact old chain engagement. Record tooth wear/damage and both original sprocket faces against OEM196/394; verify new13T/51T part identities, matching520 non-sealed114-link chain and joining components. Remove the front sprocket cover, keeping the original chain and rear wheel installed.
verification: Replacement pair and114-link chain identified
Old chain/brake can provide stationary holding

steps.title: Release the front nut while the old drive remains assembled
steps.instruction: Unfold the old washer tabs clear of the nut flats. Following Nick Dole's manual method, have the helper hold the rear brake firmly while you use a correctly fitting socket and hand breaker bar to loosen the front nut. Keep the transmission neutral and both wheels/chain installed. Stop if the chain skips or the bike/support moves. Leave the loosened nut fitted until chain removal.
verification: Old tab released before nut rotation
Nut loosened without chain slip or unstable support

source_links.title: Nick Dole: manual rear-brake holding technique, page120

steps.title: Remove the old chain
steps.instruction: Raise and securely support the rear wheel. Loosen the axle nut and both adjuster locknuts; turn adjusters inward evenly. Remove the old clip, plate and joining link, then remove the chain from its original guide/slider path. Do not run the engine to move it.
verification: Old chain removed; new joining components kept separate

steps.title: Remove the rear wheel
steps.instruction: Support the wheel, remove its nut and axle, and retain both pullers and side collars in identified positions. Lower the wheel clear of its caliper/bracket guide. The chain is already removed. Keep brake hydraulics closed and prevent pedal operation while the disc is absent.
verification: Wheel/collars/pullers identified
Brake not operated with disc absent

steps.title: Check the mounting parts
steps.instruction: Inspect axle straightness, wheel/hub, side collars, bearings, brake disc and rear sprocket mating face/hardware. Record damage or looseness; do not straighten a bent axle or reuse a damaged mounting surface.
verification: Original hub, axle, bearings and brake remain serviceable

steps.title: Remove the worn rear sprocket
steps.instruction: Support the wheel without loading its disc. Record bolt/washer arrangement and sprocket orientation. Hold each bolt while removing its self-locking nut, then remove all six fasteners and the sprocket. Clean the hub mating face.
verification: Six fastener positions accounted for
Clean undamaged mounting face

steps.title: Fit the new51-tooth sprocket
steps.instruction: Fit the exact newB2W-25451-00 sprocket in OEM orientation on the clean hub face. Restore correct bolts/washers and matching new self-locking nuts. Tighten the six nuts progressively in a crisscross pattern to42Nm while holding bolt heads. Confirm full face seating.
verification: Correct51T part/orientation
All six nuts42Nm and sprocket fully seated

steps.title: Remove the worn front sprocket
steps.instruction: Remove the previously loosened nut and discard the old lock washer. Slide off the old sprocket, keeping the original orientation identified. Inspect output-shaft splines and threads and the sprocket seating area. Damage or leakage needs its separate repair before closure.
verification: Shaft threads/splines and seat serviceable

steps.title: Locate the new13-tooth sprocket
steps.instruction: Fit exact9383E-13233 in the orientation shown by OEM196 cross-section. Install the new matching lock washer correctly engaged, then fit the nut by hand to retain the assembly. Leave washer tabs unfolded. Final locking agent, torque and tab folding occur after the new chain and wheel are installed.
verification: Correct13T sprocket and new washer located
Final torque remains pending

steps.title: Refit the wheel with the brake correctly located
steps.instruction: Grease axle and wheel seal lips with lithium-soap grease. Return each collar to its correct side, lift the wheel with its disc between the pads and locate the complete caliper bracket in the swingarm guide. Install left puller and axle from the left; fit right puller, washer and nut, leaving final tightening for chain adjustment.
verification: Correct collars/pullers and caliper guide engagement

steps.title: Join the new chain
steps.instruction: Route the matching new114-link chain around both new sprockets and the stock slider/guide. Install its matching joining link and plate with a new matching clip: closed end leads in chain travel direction per OEM198. Confirm clip engagement in both pin grooves and free joint movement. Lubricate chain without contaminating tire or brake.
verification: New114-link chain and matching joint
Clip fully seated and correctly directed

steps.title: Set measured chain slack
steps.instruction: With rear wheel raised and transmission neutral, pull chain upward with about50N above the chain-guide mounting bolt. At the exact OEM111/112 reference, measure chain-guide-to-chain-bottom distance. Adjust both sides equally to50–60mm and seat pullers against swingarm ends.
verification: Measured50–60mm and equal adjustment recorded

steps.title: Secure the rear wheel before brake-reaction torque
steps.instruction: Tighten rear axle nut to135Nm and both adjuster locknuts to21Nm. Recheck measured slack. Confirm the caliper bracket is located and pedal now has normal firm braking action with disc installed.
verification: Axle135Nm, locknuts21Nm
Brake operates normally and slack remains correct

steps.title: Torque and mechanically retain the front sprocket
steps.instruction: Remove the hand-fitted front nut without disturbing the washer/sprocket. Apply OEM-specified LOCTITE to the nut as shown, recording actual product and its instructions because Yamaha gives no grade/cure time. Refit and tighten to90Nm using the same helper-held rear brake and manual torque reaction, engine off and neutral. Firmly fold the new washer tabs against nut flats only after torque. Keep chain and axle installed and secure throughout.
verification: Front nut90Nm with recorded locking agent
New washer tabs securely against flats

source_links.title: Nick Dole: manual rear-brake holding technique, page120

steps.title: Restore the sprocket cover
steps.instruction: Refit the cover and tighten its bolts to7Nm. Remove all holding tools, parts and supports that interfere with hand wheel rotation.
verification: Cover7Nm; no tool remains in drive

steps.title: Verify the complete new drive
steps.instruction: Rotate the wheel by hand through several chain positions. Recheck50–60mm slack, chain tracking, master clip seating/direction, both sprocket mountings and normal rear-brake action. Record new part identities, all torques and final slack. Resolve binding, skipping or misalignment before use; comply with the selected locking-agent instructions before loading the joint.
verification: Both sprockets and chain replaced together
Free movement/alignment, retention and final measurements recorded

supplemental_sources.attribution: Nick Dole, Transmoto On The Tools: Gearing, hosted by Teknik Motorsport
supplemental_sources.scope: PDF5 printed120 manual rear-brake countershaft holding and unfolded tab technique only. Exact Yamaha torques, geometry and retention control. No heat, impact, chain-on-case jamming, silicone or alternative chain recommendations adopted.
